name: sharp_rademacher_singularity
statement: For B_n an n x n matrix with iid uniform {-1,+1} entries: Pr(det B_n = 0) = (1+o(1)) * 2 n^2 2^{-n} as n -> infinity.
notes: Dossier executive verdict: OPEN PROGRAM - SUBSTANTIAL AUDITED PROGRESS. The recovered packet contains no complete proof and 'must not be cited as a proof of the full conjecture' (p.1). Extraction '2n22-n' reconstructed as 2 n^2 2^{-n}.

name: antipodal_sign_fibre
statement: A sign fibre is a nonempty set A \subseteq {\pm 1}^r with A = -A (antipodal), usually assumed spanning (spans R^r) and full closed.
notes: Central deterministic object of Layer II.

name: entropy_defect_ell
statement: For X uniform on a sign fibre A \subseteq {\pm 1}^r: H(X) = log_2 |A|, and the entropy defect is \ell(A) := r - H(X) = r - log_2 |A|, the number of bits lost relative to the full cube.
notes: In the random-matrix application, \ell is the entropy budget available to pay for algebraic coincidences; converting it into residual directions is the packet's main difficulty (p.5).

name: sign_form_fibre_S
statement: General bridge formulation: given sign-valued linear forms h_a, set S = {x in {\pm 1}^r : h_a . x in {\pm 1} for every a}, with |S| = 2^{r-\ell} defining \ell. Rows already equal to signed coordinates are harmless and may be discarded before constructing the two-shadow graph.
notes: The 'two-shadow graph' is referenced but not defined within pp.1-18 (defined in later dossier pages).

name: full_dual
statement: For a sign fibre A spanning a real vector space, the full dual D(A) is the collection of linear forms taking only the values \pm 1 on A, considered projectively up to sign. A displayed coordinate family is coordinate-full when it exhausts this projective full dual.

name: closure_full_closed
statement: cl(A) = {y in {\pm 1}^r : g(y) in {\pm 1} for every g in D(A)}; the fibre is full closed when A = cl(A). Closure is intrinsic.
notes: Purpose: prevents an argument from silently ignoring extra sign points compatible with every available equation.

name: coordinate_basis
statement: A coordinate basis is a linear basis drawn from the full dual D(A). The selector distance d_cb optimizes over residual spaces AND over these bases; selected dense witness rows can sometimes replace coordinate directions.
notes: Dossier's recorded danger: basis exchange does NOT imply that all unselected rows become cheap.

name: geometric_distance_dgeo
statement: Let F = {f_i} be the projective coordinate forms on a fibre. A geometric residual space is R = span{f_i - sigma f_j : sigma in {\pm 1}}; k_F(R) is the number of signed projective classes of the f_i modulo R (all forms in R form a single zero class). d_geo = the minimum residual dimension that leaves no more classes than the ambient rank permits.

name: selector_distance_dcb
statement: Choose a coordinate basis from the full dual and assign every full-dual form to a signed basis representative; the residuals of all assignments must lie in a common space R. d_cb(A) = min dim R, minimized over both the basis and the selectors.
notes: Stronger than d_geo; the explicit basis selectors are what the centered-moment encoding needs (p.7).

name: conditional_defect_LQW
statement: A nonroot block carries incoming boundary signs W and private signs Q = (Q_1, ..., Q_q). The conditional entropy loss is L_{Q|W} = q - H(Q | W). Boundary-only forms are assigned to the parent; conditional defects then telescope down the recursive block tree.
notes: Telescoping is why a uniform rooted theorem would globalize with one absolute constant (p.8).

name: connector_absorption
statement: Ancestors may already have paid a residual subspace R_< \subseteq span W. Connector absorption is the requirement R \cap span W \subseteq R_<: any pure boundary residual created by the child must already have been paid by the parent.
notes: Not bookkeeping decoration: without it the same boundary direction can be charged at each generation, a depth loss even when every local quotient bound is linear (p.8).

name: affine_state_sets_B0_B2_M
statement: B_0 = {eta in {\pm 1}^{12} : sum_i eta_i = 0}, B_2 = {eta : sum_i eta_i = 2}; |B_0| = 924, |B_2| = 792. M = the three one-minority states of three signs.

name: exceptional_sets_Omega0_Omega1
statement: Omega_0 = B_0 x M and Omega_1 = (B_0 x {xi(1), xi(2)}) \cup (B_2 x {xi(3)}), where xi(1), xi(2), xi(3) are the one-minority states forming M.
notes: Derived sizes (digester arithmetic, consistent with the profile table): |Omega_0| = 3*924 = 2772 (the maximum profile), |Omega_1| = 2*924 + 792 = 2640; both exceed the 2592 threshold while the runner-up profile 2436 does not.

name: shared_h_homogenization_setup
statement: C = (c_1, ..., c_m) in R^{3 x m}, S_t = {x in {\pm 1}^m : Cx = t}, W = ker C, old coordinate forms f_i = x_i|_W. Homogenize: C-hat = [C | -t], W-hat = ker C-hat, h = the last coordinate form. Antipodal homogenized fibre A-hat_t = {(x,1) : x in S_t} \cup {(-x,-1) : x in S_t} = W-hat \cap {\pm 1}^{m+1}. Row rank three gives dim W-hat = m-2 = dim W + 1.
notes: Extraction glyphs 'bC', 'cW', 'bAt' are hats (C-hat, W-hat, A-hat). Delicate issue: descending a low-dimensional residual plane from W-hat to the affine fibre - the homogenizer can share a quotient class with an old form, and restriction to h = 0 may create or remove mergers; the shared-h analysis classifies the only saturated pattern in which the homogeneous corank-three theorem does not immediately descend.

name: global_bridge_dcb_exponential
statement: For every sign fibre (spanning, full-closed, antipodal; formulated generally from sign-valued linear forms): d_cb(A) <= 9 * 4^{\ell(A)} + \ell(A).
notes: Audit-ledger verdict 'New theorem'; the strongest unconditional global estimate in the packet. Extraction '9 4\ell(A) + \ell(A)' reconstructed as 9*4^{\ell}+\ell, cross-confirmed by p.3 ('9 . 4\ell + \ell') and the p.9 summable-range condition. Ledger also records 'a conditional exponential analogue' whose precise statement lies beyond pp.1-18. Proof lives in later dossier pages; this digest records the audited statement.

name: bounded_congestion_quotient
statement: For conditional blocks admitting an entropy-normalized batching with congestion kappa, the packet proves the genuinely linear quotient estimate dim((R + span W)/span W) <= (2 kappa + 1) L_{Q|W}.
notes: Audit ledger: Pass. Connector absorption is characterized separately and is NOT implied by this bound (p.3, p.8). Extraction 'dim R + span W / span W' is a displayed quotient-dimension fraction.

name: dgeo_le_dcb
statement: Always d_geo(A) <= d_cb(A). The rooted NAE family shows equality can hold nontrivially at high corank.
notes: Essential distinction for the global programme: a purely geometric quotient may merge the right classes yet fail to provide the explicit basis selectors needed by the centered-moment encoding.

name: shared_h_integration_bridge
statement: Affine spanning plus coordinate-full homogenization yields an intrinsic spanning, antipodal, full-closed cube model. Consequently the finite m <= 7 enumeration is a theorem about the original affine fibre, not merely an experiment on a chosen coordinate presentation.

name: absorption_kernel_criterion
statement: The structured linear-rigidity report gives an exact kernel criterion for connector absorption (an exact characterization of when R \cap span W \subseteq R_< can be achieved).
notes: Recorded from the p.8 summary; the criterion's full statement is on later dossier pages (S14). Paired there with the NAE-star counterexample showing bounded support alone does not suffice.

name: rooted_nae_cycles_solved
statement: Rooted NAE cycles are solved exactly, including activation-cell and connector-compatible certificates (and exact linear certificates). Although genuinely high-corank and three-connected, they do not belong to the remaining open class; the family also witnesses d_geo = d_cb nontrivially at high corank.
source: dossier p.2-3, p.7, p.10 (packet S12 per context; ledger S1-S14)
notes: Positive side of the disproved three-connected ceiling: the violating family is itself fully solved.

name: local_reduction_scope
statement: Audited reductions eliminate, before the open high-corank core: acyclic tails and globally compatible private pivots; every nonsingleton Gale-flag layer; circuit trees, sparse-cycle blocks, bounded or growing stars, and low-rank shared-form blocks; stable-set, poset, median, and paired-Gale classes (earlier project tree); boundary-closed homogeneous cyclic cores of relation corank <= 4; the named affine corank-four endpoint profiles (after the repaired 12+3 coupling); the rank-three shared-homogenizer obstruction including its exact m = 8 and m <= 7 endpoints.
notes: Layer I scope as audited; each item traces to source files reproduced on dossier pp.55-200.

name: surviving_core_localization
statement: After the audited removals, the first homogeneous survivor is a singleton-layer strongly connected cyclic component of relation corank at least five, which either has no useful low-congestion batching or fails connector absorption; the open deterministic block is dense, cyclic, singleton-layer, and connector-incoherent in every useful basis.
source: dossier p.10 (also p.4, p.9) (packet S1, S6)
notes: Called one of the most important outcomes: replaces an amorphous global gap by a sharply characterized family.

name: affine_12_3_upper_dichotomy
statement: Target-uniform repaired upper dichotomy: if a twelve-coordinate layer and a three-coordinate layer in an adapted rank-four flag have more than 2592 joint sign assignments, then either the coefficient row space already contains a four-coordinate relation with four equal nonzero magnitudes, or, after reorientation, the literal upper state set is Omega_0 = B_0 x M or Omega_1 = (B_0 x {xi(1),xi(2)}) \cup (B_2 x {xi(3)}). Both orderings 12+3 and 3+12 are treated.
notes: Stating literal state sets avoids the invalid homogeneous shortcut: the earlier zero-target/reversal argument did not control arbitrary affine targets.

name: scalar_atom_gaps
statement: Target-uniform scalar bounds: (a) for twelve nonzero coefficients, any affine atom that is not the central atom of twelve equal magnitudes has size <= 792 - unequal-magnitude case via a four-Sperner family with sum of four largest ranks C(10,5)+2C(10,4)+C(10,3) = 252+420+120 = 792; equal magnitudes with noncentral target give at most C(12,5) = 792; (b) for three signs, an affine atom has size 3 only for three equal magnitudes at a one-minority target, otherwise size <= 2. Hence a joint count above 2592 forces both own-layer rows to be equimodular: otherwise the product is at most 3*792 = 2376 or 2*924 = 1848.
notes: All binomial arithmetic digester-verified. These scalar gaps are the analytic part of the repair; the finite profile checker is used only after this target-uniform reduction. Extraction control byte at C(12,5) is a big-delimiter glyph, no content lost.

name: conditional_pair_completion
statement: Let T be an arbitrary real lower statistic and s an arbitrary target, with the lower equal pair contributing the completion kernel (1,2,1). Then: T nonconstant on Omega_0 implies N_s(T; Omega_0) <= 4788, and T nonconstant on Omega_1 implies N_s(T; Omega_1) <= 4776. Uniform in both T and s. Unequal-coefficient case: conditioning on the other ten signs gives at most C(10,5)*3 + 2*C(10,6)*2 = 756 + 840 = 1596 weighted completions per upper minority state, and 3*1596 = 4788; equal coefficients: nonidentical translates of the (1,2,1) kernel give the smaller 4776 bound for Omega_1.
notes: This conditional-counting step is the repair replacing the earlier unsupported coupling shortcut; it assumes neither target zero nor reversal symmetry. Arithmetic digester-verified.

name: constancy_forces_support_two
statement: Alternative to the counting loss: if the lower statistic T is constant on the exceptional upper state set, slice exchanges (swapping one +1 and one -1 on B_0) force all twelve coefficients to agree modulo the preceding upper rows, and comparing the three one-minority states controls the three-coordinate coefficients; hence the upper coefficient row lies in the span of the two prior upper rows. Subtracting that combination leaves a nonzero old row supported only on the lower equal pair - a support-two relation forbidden in the projectively simple configuration. So every case gives either the 4788/4776 counting loss or an immediate structural contradiction.
notes: Stronger than classifying the maximum profile: explains why an apparent equality case cannot survive as a new affine obstruction.

name: endpoint_closure_m19_m18
statement: At m = 19 the flag threshold is (81/4096)*2^{19} = 10368, and two pair completions contribute at most 2*4788 = 9576 < 10368; hence the complete-flag profiles (2,2,3,12) and (2,2,12,3) close, and constancy cannot create an equality case (it yields the forbidden support-two row). At m = 18 the threshold is (81/4096)*2^{18} = 5184 and already 4788 < 5184, validating the cited {1,2}-line uses for both 3+12 and 12+3 tails; the separate last-five profiles, where equality in a 2+3 block again forces a support-two relation, are also treated.
notes: Scope deliberately limited: the audit closes the NAMED invocations only, not unrelated sections of the larger endpoint files. Threshold extraction '81 4096 2 19' reconstructed as (81/4096)*2^19; digester-verified 81*128 = 10368, 81*64 = 5184.

name: nonsummable_survivor_profile
statement: Coverage of current deterministic theorems within the moment framework: the unconditional bridge extends the summable range to fibres with 4^{\ell} = o(\ell log n); the bounded-congestion theorem independently covers any sequence admitting a useful batching with kappa = o(log n). Consequently a surviving nonsummable sequence must have BOTH moderately large defect AND high congestion in every relevant basis.
notes: [EXTRACTION-UNCERTAIN] '4\ell = o(\ell log n)' read as 4^{\ell} = o(\ell * log n), dimensionally consistent with d_cb*k accounting at k = O(n/log n). Conditional on the centered-moment transfer framework, which itself remains open.

name: profile_455_reconstruction
statement: Independent exact reconstruction of the affine 12+3 upper-layer profile table: 455 profiles, 10 high, maximum = 2772, runner-up = 2436. Reversed ordering: the only high binomial triples are (924,924,924) and (924,924,792). Four constant profiles attain 2772 only at the two one-minority targets; six adjacent 11+1 profiles attain 2772 only at the central four-sign target; no unclassified offender remains.
notes: The C++ enumeration is exact for this finite table (target range contains the full unrestricted integer range; 64-bit counts far from overflow). It does NOT prove the arbitrary-real reduction or the conditional pair lemma - those remain analytic. Corrected runner-up at the twelve-sign scalar level is 792, superseding the obsolete 744; older zero-target/reversal files are superseded for this endpoint.

name: audit_12_3_reproduction
statement: Checkers rebuilt with warnings promoted to errors reproduce: m18 bad profiles=56; m19 bad profiles=32; ...; m30 bad profiles=1; m31 bad profiles=0. Affine (12+3) profiles: high=10, maximum=2772, runner_up=2436, reversed high triples=2. Affine m17 singleton 3+12: balanced table max beyond one-coordinate=756, adjacent=672. An independent implementation of the 455-profile convolution reproduced the same ten high profiles and the same two reversed triples.
notes: The audit separates exact finite arithmetic (checker-certified) from analytic completeness (four-level reduction, arbitrary-real target handling, constancy-to-row-space conclusion - written as proofs in the report).

name: shared_homogenizer_m8_m7
statement: Every surviving m = 8 shared-homogenizer normal form has an exact rank-two residual certificate; the m <= 7 closure is exhaustive.
source: dossier p.3 (audit ledger; details on later dossier pages) (packet S3, S5, S10 per context)
notes: Ledger verdict: Pass. Certificate details lie beyond pp.1-18; recorded here from the audit ledger statement.

name: three_connected_ceiling_falsified
statement: The three-connected constant-one ceiling claim is FALSE: rooted NAE cycles violate the constant-one ceiling (while nevertheless admitting exact linear, activation, and connector certificates).
notes: Removes a seductive shortcut: three-connectivity alone does not cap the relevant rank at a constant. The precise original ceiling statement appears in later dossier pages; pp.1-18 record the ledger verdict 'Disproved'.

name: nae_star_absorption_failure
statement: A fully closed NAE-star is a counterexample showing that bounded support alone does not imply connector absorption (R \cap span W \subseteq R_< can fail for bounded-support families).
notes: Identifies a hypothesis a successful rooted theorem must actually use; paired with the exact kernel criterion for absorption.

name: zero_target_reversal_coupling
statement: The earlier zero-target/reversal coupling argument for the affine 12+3 endpoints fails: it did not control arbitrary affine targets (invalid homogeneous shortcut), its printed summary omitted targets, and it carried an obsolete runner-up value 744 (correct: 792). Condition of failure: any use against nonzero/arbitrary affine targets or without reversal symmetry.
source: dossier p.11, p.13, p.14 (packet S1, S2)
notes: The ROUTE is invalid, not the endpoint conclusions: the target-uniform repair (dichotomy + conditional pair completion + constancy lemma) subsequently closed the named m=19/m=18 invocations. Older zero-target/reversal files are treated as superseded.

name: connector_compatible_linear_rigidity
statement: Missing deterministic bridge: a connector-compatible LINEAR entropy-rigidity theorem for dense, singleton-layer, strongly connected cyclic blocks of relation corank >= 5 with high congestion in every relevant basis - i.e. selectors achieving dim((R + R_<)/R_<) <= C * L_{Q|W} together with connector absorption R \cap span W \subseteq R_<, for one absolute constant C. By telescoping of conditional defects, a uniform rooted theorem of this form would globalize through the recursive block tree.
source: dossier p.2, p.4, p.8-10 (packet S1, S6, S9)
notes: The dossier's exact next target on the deterministic side. Not an aesthetic strengthening: it is the bridge needed to make the negative entropy term dominate all residual encoding costs uniformly (p.9).

name: centered_moment_jss_transfer
statement: Remaining probabilistic step, separate from and after the deterministic bridge: insert the deterministic component estimate into the required-order centered-moment expansion, or complete the random-normal endpoint inversion in the structured/unstructured (Jain-Sah-Sawhney) framework. The packet explicitly warns that completing Layer II alone is not yet the determinant theorem.
source: dossier p.2, p.4 (packet S1, S6, S9)

name: three_layer_architecture
statement: Layer I (local classification): encode a structured singularity mechanism as a sign fibre; remove acyclic tails, private pivots, nonsingleton flag layers, sparse cycles, star classes, low relation-corank cores (repaired 12+3 lemma and shared-h theorem close the last named affine endpoints). Layer II (global deterministic rigidity): for spanning full-closed antipodal A \subseteq {\pm 1}^r, control d_cb(A) by \ell(A) - exponential control for every fibre, linear for bounded-congestion blocks; recursion requires the rooted estimate dim((R+R_<)/R_<) <= C L_{Q|W} with R \cap span W \subseteq R_<. Layer III (probabilistic transfer): centered-moment expansion or random-normal endpoint inversion.
notes: Programme architecture, not itself a claim; its value is localizing the remaining uncertainty to the dense cyclic connector-incoherent class. Layers I-II contain proved/audited components recorded separately.

name: entropy_rigidity_reduction
statement: Component encoding in the determinant argument: leading saving proportional to -(n-r)\ell, against a selector-complexity error of schematic form O(d_cb * k + (k-r) log r + r + n). A bound d_cb = O(\ell) makes the residual cost commensurate with the entropy loss; in the endpoint range k = O(n / log n) it is small enough to preserve the required exponential saving.
notes: [EXTRACTION-UNCERTAIN] error-term grouping: raw text 'O dcbk + (k-r) log r + r + n' with a big-delimiter glyph closing the O(.); read as O(dcb*k + (k-r)log r + r + n). Schematic form only on p.9; this reduction is why d_cb = O(\ell) is THE deterministic bottleneck.

name: audit_scope_discipline
statement: Audit conventions of the dossier: exact checkers certify finite classifications and are never substituted for analytic reductions; analytic steps are written as proofs; audits close only the NAMED invocations so a local PASS is not mistaken for a global proof; counterexamples are retained as positive information identifying the hypotheses a successful theorem must use; pages 55-200 reproduce all sources with line numbers so every summary statement is traceable.
notes: Methodological convention, not a mathematical claim; governs how every status in this digest should be read.
